description: Open/close slider for gripper models in the Helping Hands design viewer. Jake (voice): 'For these gripper models, I'd like to be able to have a scroll bar and scroll them shut or open, so I can see kind of what they'll come to. They should come to a point at the tips, but then most of the rest of them will also be connected.' Asks: (1) a slider that animates each gripper design between fully open and fully closed; (2) design check: when closed, the fingers should meet at a point at the tips and most of the rest of the finger length should also make contact. Fix designs that don't.

results.identified_issue: Gallery pipeline (publish_designs.py, cad/mobile_gallery/gallery.js, index.html) is untracked WIP from another session; I added the slider hooks there (import poses.js, motionFor/applyExplosion pose transform, #pose control, ?open= preset) but did not commit those files, per the commit-own rule. If they get committed by their owner the slider comes along; if they are discarded, re-add the hooks. poses.js is .js (not .json) because publish_designs.py only copies html/js/css/svg/png from cad/mobile_gallery; the check script parses its JSON body. Hinge convention for every gen: OpenSCAD placed(s,a) = translate([s*pivot,0,0]) rotate([0,s*a,0]) — rotation about +Y, 0 = closed for v003–v006; demo_gripper exports at a=0 with 30° open_max, and gen_00's B pair is parked at x+140 (pivots 128/152). v004 yoke z=2+20 sin a, crank angle -asin((slider_z-5.746)/6) about (0,-20,-30). Check metric: per 1 mm Z slice, min X of right jaw minus max X of left jaw (projection over Y, so conservative), ignoring the first 15 mm above the pivot; 'touching' = gap ≤ 1.5 mm; PASS needs tip ≤1.5 mm and ≥60% touching. No design reaches gap ≤ 0 at the 0° stop (hence 'never touches' in the output). Deliberately did not reshape Gen 6 because it conflicts with Jake's explicit voice-650be16a correction (tip-only contact).
results.summary: Added a Closed ↔ Open slider to the design gallery for every gripper generation, plus a check that measures how each one closes. Gen 3–6 only meet at the tips. Gen 6 does that because of your earlier note. Before I reshape it: do you want the fingers to touch along their length now?
results.detailed_description:
Slider: open the design gallery (HelpingHands › Live Preview) and use the new Closed ↔ Open bar at the bottom left. It moves every generation on screen together, from fully closed to fully open, and still works with Explode, the single-gen view and orbiting. It covers all six gripper generations. Gen 4's yoke and servo crank also move with the jaws. Adding ?open=0 to the URL opens the page at the closed position.

How it works: a new file, cad/mobile_gallery/poses.js, lists each generation's hinges. Each entry gives the pivot, the angle the STLs were exported at, the range of motion, and which parts swing (matched by part name). I copied the pivots and angles by hand from each gripper.scad, so a new generation needs its own entry or its fingers won't move. If a part gets renamed it stops moving, but nothing breaks.

Closure check: Scripts/check_gripper_closure.py closes each design on the same meshes the gallery shows. It then measures the gap between the two fingers every millimetre along their length. Results at the closed stop:
- Gen 6: tips 1.2 mm apart; 8% of the 97 mm finger touching; gap at the knee up to 34 mm.
- Gen 5: tips 1.3 mm apart; 8% touching; gap up to 18 mm.
- Gen 4: tips 1.2 mm apart; 10% touching.
- Gen 3: tips 2.0 mm apart; 0% touching.
- Gen 2 (fin-ray): faces flat together; 86% touching.
- Gen 1: 58–70% touching.
So Gens 3–6 come to a point but stay open along most of the finger, and the two older demo grippers are the opposite.

What I did NOT change: the Gen 6 finger shape. During Gen 6 you said about the closed photo, 'It's not touching along most of the finger, it's just the tip here. Copy that.' That's why Gen 6 has the 7–36 mm cup gap. This note asks for most of the finger to touch, so the two notes conflict, and Gen 6 is still waiting for your review. Tell me which you want. Option one: reshape Gen 6's inner edge so the tips meet first and the rest closes flat. That's mainly filling in the knee curve; the outside hook shape stays. Option two: keep the cup gap. I'd only fix the newest generation, not the older ones.

Caveats: the slider edits sit in the gallery's gallery.js and index.html, which are uncommitted work from another session. I edited them but didn't commit them; only poses.js and the check script are committed. The live gallery already runs the new code. I tested it in headless Chrome on desktop and at phone width, not on a real phone.
results.user_reply_draft: Hey Jake, the gallery has an open/close slider now. Drag the bar at the bottom left and every gripper generation swings shut together. One thing before I change any finger shapes: Gens 3–6 only touch at the tips when closed. Gen 6 has a 34 mm gap at the knee, because during Gen 6 you said 'just the tip here, copy that.' Do you want me to flatten Gen 6's inner edge so most of the finger touches too, or keep the gap for cups?

summary: The Helping Hands design viewer needs a slider that animates each gripper model between fully open and fully closed. When closed, the finger tips should meet at a point and most of each finger's length should touch, with any designs that don't meet this fixed.
